title: How a Bengaluru eco-skincare brand stopped apologising for ₹899 and pushed repeat rate from 19% to 38%
content: SITUATION: A Bengaluru eco-skincare brand sold cold-pressed serums at ₹899 while Mamaearth-style rivals sat at ₹399. Its Meta ads screamed '100% natural, plastic-free' and converted at 0.9% CVR on a ₹540 CAC against a ₹1,150 AOV. Repeat rate was a weak 19%. Values were leading; the wallet wasn't following because 'sustainable' read as a tax, not a benefit. ACTION: We re-anchored the funnel from virtue to outcome. The hero line became 'Visible glow in 4 weeks, or full refund', with sustainability demoted to the proof layer (refillable glass, 71% less plastic) shown third, never first. We ran founder-led WhatsApp broadcasts to 14,000 past buyers offering a refill subscription at ₹749, and shifted 40% of the ₹3L/month Meta budget into retention. On Amazon.in we added before/after A+ content and seeded 200 verified reviews. OUTCOME: Over 90 days, Meta CTR doubled from 0.8% to 1.8%, CAC fell from ₹540 to ₹410, AOV rose to ₹1,420 via refill bundling, and repeat rate climbed from 19% to 38%. Blended ROAS moved from 2.1 to 3.4. The premium held; nothing was discounted.
lesson: Values-led positioning only sells the premium when the benefit leads and the values prove it. Put the customer outcome first (result plus refund guarantee), make sustainability the credibility layer, then convert one-time buyers into refill subscribers so the price is justified over a lifetime of carts, not a single one. Discounting would have trained the buyer to wait; subscription trained them to return.
